chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I may be on a journey, and the time for salat (prayer) comes while I do not have water with me, and it is said that water is near us. Should I search for water to my right and left while I am still within the time? He said: Do not search for water; rather, perform tayammum, for I fear that you may fall behind your companions, become lost, and a beast may devour you.
Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, said: Al-ṣaʿīd is dust, and it is only called ṣaʿīd because it rises from the earth upon its surface, and al-ṭayyib is that in which no impurity is known.

What Ibn Durayd mentioned in the book al-Jamharah from Abū ʿUbaydah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā indicates this: that al-ṣaʿīd is pure dust not mixed with saline soil or sand, and his statement is authoritative in language.

Because the intended meaning can only be one of three things: dust, the earth itself, or what rises upon the earth. If the first is intended, then what we have said is established. If the second is intended, then what our opponents from among the companions of Abū Ḥanīfah have held also does not enter into it, because kohl and arsenic are not unconditionally called earth, just as the rest of the minerals such as silver, gold, and iron are not called earth. Do you not see that one who has some kohl or arsenic does not say, “I have a piece of earth”? Thus it is known that the name of earth is not applied to it.

And if what is intended by it is what rises upon the earth, then it can only mean either what rises upon it from its own kind or what is not from its own kind. If the first is intended, then what we mentioned is established. If the second is intended, then it is false, because among what rises upon the earth are things to which the name al-ṣaʿīd is not applied, such as fruits, minerals, and everything outside the genus of the earth.

Then he said: It is recommended that tayammum be performed from elevated ground and the high parts of the land from which waters run down, for they are purer than their low-lying places. This is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: the earth-surface dust used for tayammum
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat (prayer) whose time has arrived
key_terms.تَيَمَّمْ: perform tayammum, the dry ablution in place of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler perform tayammum instead of searching for water?
ai.summary: This text gives a ruling on tayammum during travel when seeking water may put a person in danger or cause separation from companions. It also explains the meaning of al-ṣaʿīd as pure dust or earth-surface material suitable for tayammum, and discusses the linguistic basis for excluding minerals and other non-earth substances.
